Dermatology · published research

Herpes labialis

A meta-analysis of six randomized trials favored PBM for short-term pain, healing time, and lesion size, although individual trials differ and most included trials had high risk of bias. Recurrence prevention is supported by fewer studies.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A meta-analysis of six randomized trials favored PBM for short-term pain, healing time, and lesion size, although individual trials differ and most included trials had high risk of bias. Recurrence prevention is supported by fewer studies.

Summary of the Evidence

The category contains 23 records: 18 human reports, four evidence syntheses, and one in-vitro paper. Human reports include 11 randomized-trial publications, three case reports, and four case series. One includes longer follow-up, and reviews reuse overlapping trial cohorts. Some reports combine PBM with photodynamic therapy, so records are not 23 independent treatment studies.

Human and clinical evidence

A 2025 meta-analysis pooled six randomized trials with 260 participants. Results favored PBM for pain on days 2 and 3, healing time by about 1.22 days, and lesion size on day 3. Five trials were judged at high risk of bias, so these pooled estimates remain uncertain (Yang et al. 2025).

Individual trials differ by outcome. In a double-blind study of 40 people, 650-nm red light reduced pain faster than acyclovir cream, but healing time did not differ (Al-Hallak et al. 2024). A 22-person trial added PBM to acyclovir and reported lower pain on days 2 and 3 and smaller lesions on days 7 and 10 (Seyyedi et al. 2024).

Recurrence prevention is distinct from treating an active lesion. A sham-controlled trial of 158 people followed participants for two years after six months of treatment. Both 808-nm groups had fewer or less severe recurrences than placebo, with the lower fluence reported as more satisfactory. Photodynamic treatment was also used for outbreaks during treatment, separate from preventive PBM (Zanella et al. 2022).

Animal evidence

No animal study was identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One in-vitro report examined laser effects on an E. coli plasmid. It is not an HSV model and does not demonstrate antiviral activity against herpes simplex virus.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols include 650-nm red light at 4.7 J/cm² for 120 seconds, 940-nm near-infrared light added to acyclovir, and 808-nm near-infrared light at 11.11 or 22.22 J/cm² for prevention. A 2025 trial combined antimicrobial photodynamic therapy with PBM, not PBM alone; its report conflicts between 650-nm red and 980-nm near-infrared. No optimal protocol is established across treatment and prevention.

Interpretation

Randomized evidence and a pooled analysis favor short-term pain and healing, but the trial set is small and risk of bias matters. Recurrence prevention has fewer independent data. Photodynamic co-treatment complicates some reports.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for short-term pain relief and lesion healing Low for prevention of recurrences
Publications and records23 articles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Several randomized trials and a recent meta-analysis support short-term pain or healing benefits, although the pooled trial set is small and most trials in that analysis had high risk of bias. Recurrence prevention has fewer studies and uses a different treatment schedule. Larger sham-controlled trials with standardized outcomes, separate acute and preventive protocols, and longer follow-up would support stronger conclusions.
